prompt: In many countries, public confidence in politicians has fallen sharply in recent decades. What has caused this loss of trust? How might it be rebuilt?
essay:
Confidence in elected representatives has weakened across much of the democratic world, and the explanation is neither simple dishonesty nor a sudden change in the character of politicians. In my view the decline has two main sources, and any attempt to reverse it has to deal with both.

The first is the gap between what campaigns promise and what governments can deliver. Politicians competing for office have every incentive to describe their intentions in confident, specific terms, yet much of what determines outcomes — global prices, court rulings, the decisions of previous administrations — lies outside their control. Voters who were promised certainty and given excuses conclude, reasonably enough, that they were misled rather than merely disappointed.

The second is visibility. Information that once circulated only among journalists is now available instantly and in full, so that every expenses claim and every awkward recording reaches the public directly. This does not mean politicians behave worse than their predecessors; it means the evidence is no longer filtered. The effect is nonetheless corrosive, because scandals accumulate in the memory while the routine competence of government goes unrecorded.

Rebuilding trust therefore depends on narrowing the gap and managing the visibility. Parties could be required to publish costed programmes that an independent office assesses before polling day, which would make the extravagant claims expensive to make. Transparency rules on lobbying and party funding would remove the suspicion that decisions are bought. Most importantly, governments should report honestly on the commitments they have failed to meet, since an admitted failure damages credibility far less than a quietly abandoned one.

None of this restores confidence quickly. But trust is rebuilt in the same way it is lost, through a long accumulation of small verifiable acts.
title: Why people no longer trust politicians
